root_cause.text: A race in the thermal core let suspend/resume paths reinitialize and requeue a thermal zone’s `poll_queue` delayed work during `thermal_zone_device_unregister()`, so `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` could miss in-flight or newly reinitialized work and free the `thermal_zone_device` while that work still referenced it.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that `thermal_zone_pm_complete()` and `thermal_zone_device_resume()` “re-initialize the poll_queue delayed work” causing `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` in unregister to “miss some already running work items” and leading to use-after-free; the patch moves `cancel_delayed_work()` earlier to `thermal_zone_pm_prepare()`, flushes a dedicated `thermal_wq`, and adds `if (tz->state & TZ_STATE_FLAG_EXIT) return;` in `thermal_zone_device_resume()` to stop reinitialization when the zone is being removed.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly states that `thermal_zone_pm_complete()` and `thermal_zone_device_resume()` “re-initialize the poll_queue delayed work” causing `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` in unregister to “miss some already running work items” and leading to use-after-free; the patch moves `cancel_delayed_work()` earlier to `thermal_zone_pm_prepare()`, flushes a dedicated `thermal_wq`, and adds `if (tz->state & TZ_STATE_FLAG_EXIT) return;` in `thermal_zone_device_resume()` to stop reinitialization when the zone is being removed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a global thermal workqueue pointer that is immutable after initialization to support thermal workqueue usage with post-init hardening.
intent_record.what: A new file-scope static variable `thermal_wq` of type `struct workqueue_struct *` was added, and it is annotated with `__ro_after_init` so the pointer becomes read-only after kernel initialization.
intent_record.how: This introduces storage for a global thermal subsystem workqueue pointer and hardens it by preventing reassignment after init, enabling later code to use a dedicated workqueue reference while reducing the risk of accidental or unintended modification at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the thermal subsystem workqueue for thermal zone polling instead of the generic freezable power-efficient workqueue.
intent_record.what: The call to mod_delayed_work() in thermal_zone_device_set_polling() was changed to use thermal_wq instead of system_freezable_power_efficient_wq when scheduling tz->poll_queue.
intent_record.how: Thermal zone polling work is now queued on the dedicated thermal workqueue rather than the generic freezable power-efficient workqueue, changing which worker context executes the delayed polling task and ensuring it follows the thermal subsystem's intended workqueue behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an early exit in thermal_zone_device_resume() to skip resume processing for thermal zones marked for removal.
intent_record.what: A new early-return check was added in thermal_zone_device_resume() after acquiring the thermal zone guard: it tests whether tz->state has TZ_STATE_FLAG_EXIT set, and if so returns immediately, along with a comment explaining that no work is needed if the thermal zone is going away.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the resume path from clearing suspended/resuming state or performing further resume handling on a thermal zone that is already being torn down, avoiding operations on an exiting device and reducing the chance of invalid state transitions during teardown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel pending thermal zone polling work during suspend preparation to prevent poll work from being queued or run after the zone is marked suspended.
intent_record.what: In thermal_zone_pm_prepare(), after setting tz->state |= TZ_STATE_FLAG_SUSPENDED, a new comment was added and a call to cancel_delayed_work(&tz->poll_queue) was inserted.
intent_record.how: At suspend preparation time, any pending delayed polling work for the thermal zone is canceled so it will not later be queued or executed while the zone is marked suspended, preventing new poll work from reaching the workqueue during suspend transition.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop canceling the thermal zone delayed polling work during PM completion so scheduled polling is not unnecessarily suppressed during resume handling.
intent_record.what: The call to cancel_delayed_work(&tz->poll_queue); was removed from the beginning of thermal_zone_pm_complete(), while the guard, completion reinitialization, and state flag update remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, thermal_zone_pm_complete() no longer cancels the thermal zone's pending delayed polling work during PM completion, allowing any already scheduled poll_queue work to remain active instead of being explicitly stopped at this point.

intent_record.intent_summary: Queue thermal zone resume work on the thermal subsystem workqueue instead of the generic freezable power-efficient workqueue.
intent_record.what: In thermal_zone_pm_complete(), the workqueue argument passed to mod_delayed_work() was changed from system_freezable_power_efficient_wq to thermal_wq, while keeping the same delayed work item and zero delay.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the resume-related delayed work for the thermal zone is now queued on the dedicated thermal workqueue instead of the generic freezable power-efficient workqueue, changing which execution context handles the callback and aligning post-resume thermal processing with the thermal subsystem's own worker thread.

intent_record.intent_summary: Flush the thermal workqueue during suspend and restore preparation to ensure pending thermal work completes before power-management transitions.
intent_record.what: In the PM_RESTORE_PREPARE and PM_SUSPEND_PREPARE cases of thermal_pm_notify(), a comment was added and a call to flush_workqueue(thermal_wq) was inserted immediately after thermal_pm_notify_prepare() and before the switch case break.
intent_record.how: At suspend or restore preparation time, the thermal workqueue is now synchronously drained so any pending thermal work items already queued are allowed to finish before power management continues. This prevents leftover thermal work from interfering with later suspend/resume processing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Allocate and validate the thermal event workqueue during init and unwind it correctly on later failures.
intent_record.what: In thermal_init(), a new workqueue named "thermal_events" is allocated with alloc_workqueue() using WQ_FREEZABLE | WQ_POWER_EFFICIENT | WQ_PERCPU flags before calling thermal_register_governors(); a null check was added to return -ENOMEM and jump to unregister_netlink if allocation fails; and the thermal_register_governors() error path was changed from jumping to unregister_netlink to jumping to destroy_workqueue.
intent_record.how: This change ensures the thermal subsystem creates its dedicated workqueue during initialization, cleanly aborts initialization if the allocation fails, and frees that workqueue on later initialization failure paths such as governor registration errors, preventing use of an uninitialized queue and avoiding resource leaks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Destroy the thermal workqueue on thermal_init() failure to properly clean up partially initialized resources.
intent_record.what: A new error-handling label `destroy_workqueue:` was added in `thermal_init()`, and it calls `destroy_workqueue(thermal_wq)` before continuing to the existing `unregister_netlink:` cleanup path.
intent_record.how: On initialization failure paths that jump to this new label, the thermal workqueue is now explicitly destroyed, preventing the allocated workqueue from being left behind during partial initialization rollback.

grouping_result.intent: Add a global thermal workqueue pointer that is immutable after initialization to support thermal workqueue usage with post-init hardening.
Flush the thermal workqueue during suspend and restore preparation to ensure pending thermal work completes before power-management transitions.
Add an early exit in thermal_zone_device_resume() to skip resume processing for thermal zones marked for removal.
Cancel pending thermal zone polling work during suspend preparation to prevent poll work from being queued or run after the zone is marked suspended.
Destroy the thermal workqueue on thermal_init() failure to properly clean up partially initialized resources.

consistency_review.core_intent: Align thermal zone power-management work handling with the dedicated thermal workqueue and proper suspend/resume sequencing so thermal tasks are managed correctly across PM transitions.
Ensure thermal initialization correctly manages the thermal event workqueue by allocating/validating it and cleaning it up on initialization failure paths.
Align thermal zone polling and resume work handling with the dedicated thermal workqueue and PM transition behavior so thermal work is managed correctly across suspend and resume.
Ensure thermal subsystem initialization properly creates, validates, and cleans up the thermal event workqueue on failure paths to avoid leaking partially initialized resources.
Route thermal zone polling and resume work through the thermal subsystem workqueue and manage it consistently across PM transitions so thermal work is not blocked or mishandled during suspend/resume.
Ensure thermal subsystem initialization properly manages the thermal event workqueue by creating it safely and cleaning it up on initialization failure paths.

relevance_review.reason: This change only makes the global thermal workqueue pointer immutable after initialization for hardening. It does not address the unregister/suspend-resume race where delayed work is reinitialized or requeued during thermal_zone_device_unregister(), nor the cancel_delayed_work_sync/use-after-free issue.

The changes directly affect the same thermal zone delayed work and PM suspend/resume interactions described in the root cause: they move polling/resume work onto the thermal workqueue and add PM-time flushing/consistent handling to prevent work from being requeued or left in flight during unregister and power transitions.

The change directly targets the suspend/resume side of the race by preventing thermal_zone_device_resume() from reinitializing or requeuing work for zones being removed, which addresses the use-after-free window during thermal_zone_device_unregister().

The change directly targets the thermal zone polling work race by canceling pending poll_queue work during suspend preparation, preventing suspend/resume from requeueing or running delayed work after suspension begins—the same workqueue lifetime issue underlying the unregister/use-after-free vulnerability.

These changes concern creation and cleanup of the global thermal event workqueue during subsystem initialization failure paths, not the unregister/suspend-resume race involving a thermal zone's poll_queue delayed work being reinitialized or requeued during thermal_zone_device_unregister().

candidates.rationale: Reinitializing tz->poll_queue during resume is the core unsafe action: it can race with unregister(), replacing the delayed work state while unregister is trying to cancel it, allowing work to survive and later access a freed thermal_zone_device.

This requeues the thermal zone's delayed work during PM completion/resume, creating the race where unregister() may have already canceled prior work but newly queued work still references tz after it is freed.

This non-synchronous cancellation in the PM path contributes to the race by not waiting for poll_queue work to finish, and it interacts badly with later reinitialization/requeueing of the same work item during suspend/resume transitions.

Regular polling uses the same poll_queue work item and can schedule it on a generic workqueue, so concurrent polling activity is part of the race window in which unregister() may miss in-flight or rescheduled work that still dereferences tz.

vuln_statements.explanation: This reinitializes the same delayed work item during resume. That can replace the work state while thermal_zone_device_unregister() is trying to cancel it, allowing unregister to miss the active/new work and free the thermal_zone_device while the resumed work still references it.

After reinitialization, this immediately requeues poll_queue during resume. That creates the use-after-free race described in the root cause because unregister may already have canceled earlier work, but this newly queued work can still run after the thermal_zone_device is freed.
